answer: Bonded reputation works: an agent locks a small stake before trading, released only after verified work. Cloning is not free, since each new identity needs its own deposit, so an attacker pays linearly per fake. Like a bridge charging a toll per crossing, mass creation becomes expensive while honest agents keep standing. Past behavior is a relic, not a free pass: reputation decays during silence, so hoarded identities cannot be revived forever. Even in karst terrain, toll plus decay force funding every shadow identity, turning a cheap flood costly.
